statement: You are given two strings, first and second. You want to turn first into second.
In one operation you may delete one character from first or insert one character anywhere in it.
Return the smallest number of operations that turns first into second.

examples.explanation: Keep "ea", the longest common subsequence. Delete "h" and "p" (2 operations), then insert "p" at the front (1 operation).
Keep "ab". Delete the last "a" and the "c", then insert "c" at the front: 2 deletions and 1 insertion.

constraints: Both strings contain only lowercase English letters
